issues.failure_explanation: Substituting \hat u^n = \tilde u^n into the general optimality equation yields M(y^n-\tilde u^n), not (2M/\delta t)(y^n-\tilde u^n). Thus the equation and all subsequent analysis in Section 3.2 are for a different update than the algorithm's subproblem when \hat u^n=\tilde u^n.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the coefficient \frac{2M}{\delta t} by M in \eqref{eq:til:yn} and rederive the estimates in Propositions \ref{prop:til:1}, \ref{prop:til2}, Corollary \ref{coro:til1}, and Theorems \ref{thm:square:sum:til}, \ref{thm:globalconverg:M} with the corrected M terms.
issues.overall_effect: All convergence guarantees for the case \hat u^n=\tilde u^n (Theorems \ref{thm:square:sum:til} and \ref{thm:globalconverg:M}) are not established for the algorithm as defined.
issues.title: Incorrect M coefficient in update equation for \hat u^n=\tilde u^n
issues.why_classification: The error invalidates the entire second case of the convergence analysis, which is a central claimed contribution.

issues.failure_explanation: The convergence theorems require the accepted line-search step \lambda_n to be strictly below a small \delta t,L-dependent bound. The algorithm allows any positive \bar \lambda_{\max} and does not cap the final \lambda_n by that bound. The Armijo condition can be satisfied for larger steps, so the hypotheses of the convergence theorems are not guaranteed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add an input condition or cap that enforces \lambda_n < the minimum of the bounds required in Theorems \ref{thm:globalconverg} and \ref{thm:square:sum:til} for the relevant case, or prove convergence without this bound.
issues.overall_effect: The global convergence guarantees do not apply to the algorithm as written unless the user independently chooses \bar \lambda_{\max} within the theoretical bound; the numerical experiments use \bar \lambda_{\max}=5, violating the bound.
issues.title: Algorithm does not enforce required line-search step-size bound
issues.why_classification: The main convergence guarantee is conditional on a step-size bound not enforced by the proposed algorithm.

issues.failure_explanation: The convergence proofs require y^n to be an exact critical point of the subproblem. The one-step preconditioned formula in Proposition \ref{prop:proximal_to_pre} solves the subproblem exactly only when h is affine. If only finitely many preconditioned iterations are performed without error control, the optimality condition has a nonzero residual, and the paper provides no inexact convergence analysis. Thus the claimed global convergence for the practical finite-iteration algorithm is unsupported.

failure_location.quote: By conducting a finite number of preconditioned iterations without error control, we can guarantee global convergence along with line search accelerations.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either prove convergence with inexact subproblem solves and explicit error-control/conditions, or restrict the claim to exact solves and provide an exact solver for the subproblem.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised practical guarantee that finite, error-uncontrolled preconditioned iterations retain global convergence is not established.
issues.title: Unsupported claim that finite error-uncontrolled preconditioned iterations preserve global convergence
issues.why_classification: The claim is a central advertised feature; without it, the practical algorithm's global convergence guarantee is missing.

issues.failure_explanation: For \hat u^n=\tilde u^n, d^n is not guaranteed to be a descent direction, so the standard Armijo while loop may never terminate (the inequality can fail for all positive \lambda_n). The analysis of the \tilde u case assumes the modified rule that sets \lambda_n=0 when no positive step exists. Algorithm \ref{alg:cap} does not include this fallback, so the analyzed procedure is not the one in the algorithm block.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Modify Algorithm \ref{alg:cap} to include the fallback: if no positive step satisfies the Armijo inequality, set \lambda_n=0 and u^{n+1}=y^n.
issues.overall_effect: The algorithm as written may not terminate for the \hat u^n=\tilde u^n case, and the convergence theorems for that case do not apply to it.
